about: The mutant ledger of internal/sketch/fix (ergo fix, EXPLICIT EX1): edits that TestFixProperty or TestExplicitClauseText must kill. Run it with go run ./scripts/mutants internal/sketch/fix.

mutants.name: mutfrag-no-close
mutants.rule: A signature whose body a later literal writes is respelled: closing braces are tried after a fragment.

mutants.name: mutfrag-verbs-kept
mutants.rule: A fmt format is respelled: each verb stands as text of its own length, so the format parses and every offset is kept.

mutants.name: mutfrag-lent-kept
mutants.from: all = append(all, lentEdits(f)...) // [T lent] as Mut deletes it
mutants.rule: A generator's piece is respelled as a whole source is: [T lent] loses lent (MODES-4).

mutants.rule: ergo fix --go respells the Ergo pieces in a test's or a generator's strings (MutFragment).

mutants.name: fix-fragment-test-closes
mutants.rule: A test's string literal is respelled only when it parses whole: its open pieces are Go the test expects of the lowering.

mutants.name: fix-ergo-marker-off
mutants.from: func ergoMarker(text string) bool { return ergoMarkerRE.MatchString(text) }
mutants.to: func ergoMarker(text string) bool { return false }
mutants.rule: A test's open piece of Ergo (import sync, let …) is closed and respelled as a generator's is.

mutants.rule: A source that returns a *T is Go: no Ergo function returns a borrow (types.md, Borrows 1).

mutants.name: ex1-needs-for-fails
mutants.rule: A failure is written in the fails clause, a capability in needs.

mutants.name: ex1-no-recheck
mutants.rule: Writing a callee's clause can make its callers exceed theirs: the tool checks again until no clause diagnostic is left. The loop is std code's Plan(Fixes) (SEM4b): a check after the first that offers no fix ends it.

mutants.name: ex1-after-takes
mutants.rule: A new clause goes after the results and fails, before takes (grammar.md Declarations).

mutants.name: ex1-no-import
mutants.rule: An element of a package the file does not import is written with the import it needs.

mutants.name: ex1-reorder-written
mutants.rule: Written elements keep their written order; the missing ones follow them.

mutants.name: ex1-site-row-text
mutants.rule: Every site of one clause prints the whole clause, one text.

mutants.name: lint1-fix-overlap
mutants.rule: A fix inside an earlier fix's span waits for a later round.

mutants.name: lint1-fix-keep-unused
mutants.from:
dropped, ok := dropUnused(next, out.Diagnostics, unused)
			if !ok {
mutants.to:
dropped, ok := dropUnused(next, out.Diagnostics, unused)
			if !ok || true {
mutants.rule: An import the fixes leave unused is removed.

mutants.name: lint1-fix-no-refusal
mutants.rule: A lint fix whose program does not check refuses the whole run.

mutants.name: lint1-fix-unsafe
mutants.rule: Only the findings of rules marked safe, with a fix, are applied.

mutants.name: ex2-no-open
mutants.rule: A clause written after a lone result of function type is the function's only when the result is in parentheses; otherwise it is the result type's row.

mutants.name: rel5-hide-named
mutants.rule: A clause that must name a prelude type the package hides is not written (fix would name the package's type); the S102 asks for the rename (L6, q30).

mutants.name: rel5-hide-basic
mutants.rule: A universe basic type the package hides has no spelling there.

mutants.name: rel5-hide-map
mutants.from: s.hide("Map") // the syntax's Map[K, V] (grammar.md, Parser 8)
mutants.rule: The map type has no spelling in a package that declares its own Map.

mutants.name: rel5-hide-attach
mutants.rule: The checker never attaches a clause it cannot write (q137): the S102 that asks for the rename carries none.

mutants.name: ex2-no-open-apply
mutants.from: insert{at: f.Open, text: "("}, insert{at: f.InsertAt, text: ")"}
mutants.to: insert{at: f.Open, text: ""}, insert{at: f.InsertAt, text: ""}
mutants.rule: ergo fix writes the parentheses the clause needs around a lone result of function type.

mutants.name: ex3-takes-no-fix
mutants.rule: A hand-off of a lent parameter carries the takes clause to write, which ergo fix writes (q137).

mutants.name: ex3-wire-tparam-uncharged
mutants.from: c.chargeAs(x, &Wired{T: tp, Uses: true}, fmt.Sprintf("the codec of %s, which this %s calls,", tp.Name, what))
mutants.rule: An encode or decode of a type parameter T is charged needs wired[T], so a generic codec writes it (q141).

mutants.name: ex3-instance-wired-kept
mutants.rule: An instance replaces needs wired[T] by its argument's codec needs (q141).

mutants.name: ex3-wired-needs-wire-only
mutants.rule: needs wired[T] is the needs of both directions of each by-name pair T reaches (q141).

mutants.name: ex3-wired-spelled
mutants.rule: ergo fix spells needs wired[T] (q141).

mutants.name: exc1-fix-include-keeps-members
mutants.rule: An include replaces the operations it brings, so a second fix and the checker see one operation each (audit CSX §4.10).

mutants.name: exm1-fix-split-flipped
mutants.rule: fix writes own on exactly the names a takes clause named, splitting a group taken in part in order (q168).

mutants.name: exm1-fix-law-param
mutants.rule: A law's parameter is a parameter: fix writes own for its escaping, never deletes it (q168).

mutants.name: exm1-fix-field-escaping-kept
mutants.rule: fix deletes escaping on a field's or a result's function type, which is escaping already (q168).

mutants.name: modes1-fix-binding-star
mutants.rule: fix keeps *T in a Go binding, where it is Go's pointer (q169).

mutants.name: modes2-fix-gosource
mutants.rule: ergo fix --go leaves a Go string that also parses as Ergo but names a type of a package it does not import (a Go test function) as it is (MODES-2).

mutants.name: modes4-fix-no-mut-param
mutants.rule: ergo fix writes x mut T for each parameter of a type parameter it drops lent from (MODES-4).

mutants.name: modes4-fix-bare-mut

mutants.rule: [T lent] becomes [T] with its parameters read: T has no operation to write through (MODES-4).

mutants.name: modes4-fix-mutop-dropped
mutants.rule: ergo fix marks mut each operation a function on mut T implemented through [T lent C] (MODES-4).

mutants.name: fix-include-leaves-mode
mutants.rule: An include deletes the included operation from its mode word on, so no `own` or `mut` is left alone.

mutants.name: respell-gen-imports-off
mutants.rule: A generator's piece that names a package another piece imports is Ergo, and its borrow is respelled.

mutants.name: respell-typearg-rewritten
mutants.rule: A *T that binds a type parameter is left by the respell (a type parameter binds no borrow).

mutants.name: respell-typearg-functype-left
mutants.from:
case *syntax.FuncType:
					return false // its parameters take modes again
mutants.rule: A function type inside a type argument takes modes again: its borrow is respelled.

mutants.name: respell-kept-unreported
mutants.rule: RunMut prints a line for each *T it leaves.
